Pegasus · Management Reports design review · 9 October 2026

One period for every report, and the figures you came for first.

Three ways to lay out Administration › Management Reports, all on the current Pegasus shell and all drawn from the same synthetic office. Each one moves the period out of Engineer activity so it visibly governs every report, puts Person on the one report it filters, gives every report its own download, and stops an invalid period from showing zeros. Open today’s page drawn from the same data to compare.

One period bar

From, To and Apply sit under the title and govern every report; Download workbook moves to the page head. A period that ends before it starts shows the error there and draws no report, instead of zeros in Engineer activity and Unavailable elsewhere.

Narrower tables

Inspection and Audit become one Work choice per table, so Reports by Principal drops from ten columns to four and By month from twelve to six. The CSV and the workbook keep every column. A strip switch puts today’s columns back (item D).

Proposals behind the page

Strip switches add sections computed from data Pegasus already records: Queues now (Held, Triage, Unidentified), Cases by stage, Outcomes with Audit agreement, the previous period beside each total, and period presets. Each is a lettered item; none needs new recording.

A

Tidied sections

Today’s four reports, one period bar, narrower tables.

The page keeps its four sections in their order. The period moves out of Engineer activity into one bar under the title that governs every section, and Person sits on the one section it filters. Inspection and Audit become one Work choice per table, so the 10- and 12-column tables drop to four and six. Every section has its own Download CSV in its head; Download workbook moves to the page head.

Why choose it
Nothing is lost or moved far: an Administrator who knows today’s page finds every figure where it was. It is the smallest Stage 2.
Tradeoff
Still one long page: Turnaround and the Case list sit below two wide sections, and the headline figures are spread across three tile rows.

B

Overview first

Recommended

The period’s headline figures, then one report at a time.

Five tiles give the period at a glance. A tile, or the Report choice beside it, opens one report below: Engineer activity, Reports by Principal, By month, Turnaround or the Case list. The period bar and Download workbook are shared; each report has its own Download CSV.

Why choose it
The page fits one screen at 1440; the figure you came for is one click away, and the tiles are the totals every report agrees on.
Tradeoff
Only one report is visible at a time, so comparing Turnaround against Reports by Principal needs two views or the workbook.

C

Month ledger

Whole months by Principal, for the fee notes and the invoice run.

The period is a range of whole London months. The main table is Principal by month for one chosen measure, with the month totals drawn as navy bars. Choosing a Principal opens its months, its turnaround and its held Cases under the ledger. Engineer activity, Turnaround and the Case list follow below for the same months.

Why choose it
Matches how fees are invoiced: whole months, by Principal, with the month-on-month trend visible without a spreadsheet.
Tradeoff
A period that is not whole months (a week, or a fortnight to date) cannot be asked for, and the bars are a new kind of figure for the page (item I).

Recommended: B · Overview first. It answers “what happened this period” in one row of tiles, keeps every report one choice away, and fits one screen at 1440. A is the smallest change; C suits the monthly invoice run best.
Try it: sort Engineer activity, choose a Person, switch Work to Audit, open a tile in B, choose a Principal in C’s ledger, download a CSV with Reports by Principal unavailable, and load the Monthly invoicing preset. Read the notes and the lettered sign-off items. These are offline design artifacts and do not establish how the application behaves.
